---
title: Course map
---

**Parts 0–4 are available: 27 complete lessons.** Parts 5–6 and the reference pages remain coming soon. Begin with [your first notebook](00-start/02-first-notebook.ipynb); read [0.1](00-start/01-what-python-is-for.ipynb) first if you want an overview. Plan for 20–40 minutes per lesson, including practice and breaks.

Our running question is **Do people live longer in richer countries?** We return to the same historical country panel as your skills grow. Short introductions use made-up numbers for fictional countries. The missing-data lesson also uses a clearly labelled simulated survey; it contains no actual people.

Work through the core lessons in order. Each notebook can run independently from a fresh Colab session, so it prepares any files it needs and does not depend on variables from the preceding notebook. Use the exercises before opening solutions, then restart and run from the top to check your work.

## Part 0 · Start here

- [0.1 What Python is for in social science](00-start/01-what-python-is-for.ipynb)
- [0.2 Your first notebook, in the browser](00-start/02-first-notebook.ipynb)
- [0.3 How to use this course and get unstuck](00-start/03-how-to-learn.ipynb)

Run code in your browser, understand the course's scope and practise getting unstuck. No local installation is needed.

## Part 1 · Python basics

- [1.1 Values and variables](01-basics/01-values-variables.ipynb)
- [1.2 Lists and dictionaries](01-basics/02-lists-dictionaries.ipynb)
- [1.3 Making decisions and repeating things](01-basics/03-decisions-repetition.ipynb)
- [1.4 Functions: using them and writing your own](01-basics/04-functions.ipynb)
- [1.5 Reading error messages](01-basics/05-reading-errors.ipynb)
- [1.6 Importing libraries](01-basics/06-importing-libraries.ipynb)

Move from individual values to collections, decisions, repetition, functions and library imports. Apply each idea to social-science measurements before loading a complete table.

## Part 2 · Working with data

- [2.1 Loading data and looking at it](02-data/01-loading-data.ipynb)
- [2.2 Selecting rows and columns](02-data/02-selecting.ipynb)
- [2.3 Creating and transforming variables](02-data/03-transforming.ipynb)
- [2.4 Missing values and data types](02-data/04-missing-types.ipynb)
- [2.5 Group summaries: the pivot table lesson](02-data/05-group-summaries.ipynb)
- [2.6 Combining datasets safely](02-data/06-combining.ipynb)
- [2.7 Wide and long data; panel structure](02-data/07-reshaping.ipynb)
- [2.8 Dates and time series basics](02-data/08-dates-time-series.ipynb)

Inspect CSV, Excel and Stata files; select observations; create variables; handle missing values and types; summarize groups; validate joins; reshape a panel; and check dates and time spacing.

## Part 3 · Visualization

- [3.1 First plots from a DataFrame](03-viz/01-first-plots.ipynb)
- [3.2 Making a chart readable: labels, scales and colour](03-viz/02-readable-charts.ipynb)
- [3.3 Comparing groups and small multiples](03-viz/03-groups-small-multiples.ipynb)
- [3.4 Saving figures for a paper or slides](03-viz/04-saving-figures.ipynb)

Build the income–life expectancy scatter in small steps, then compare patterns across decades. A small multiple repeats the same chart for different groups.

## Part 4 · Statistics and regression

- [4.1 Descriptive statistics and a Table 1](04-regression/01-descriptive-statistics.ipynb)
- [4.2 Correlation and simple OLS](04-regression/02-correlation-ols.ipynb)
- [4.3 Multiple regression, categories and interactions](04-regression/03-multiple-regression.ipynb)
- [4.4 Robust and clustered standard errors](04-regression/04-robust-clustered.ipynb)
- [4.5 Fixed effects and panel models](04-regression/05-fixed-effects.ipynb)
- [4.6 Regression tables you can put in a paper](04-regression/06-regression-tables.ipynb)

Learn what a model estimates and what it cannot establish. Ordinary least squares (OLS) fits a linear relationship; fixed effects account for group differences that stay constant over time. Instrumental variables and difference-in-differences are beyond the core path.
